data.name: Vihan
data.gender_notes: Vihan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vihan', meaning 'Sky', 'Heaven', 'Travel'. In Hindu mythology, Vihan is associated with the divine chariot that transports gods and goddesses. This name signifies a connection to the divine and a journey towards spiritual enlightenment. The name Vihan carries the meaning “Sky, Heaven, Travel” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vihan usually hope their child will grow to embody sky, heaven, travel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of the divine journey towards spiritual enlightenment.
data.etymology: Vihan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sky, Heaven, Travel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vihan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Vihan was a popular name for Jain monks during the 12th and 13th century CE The name Vihan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During the medieval period in India, Jainism was a major religious force and monks played an important role in its spread. The name Vihan was widely used among these monks.

historical_references.reference: Vihan is also mentioned in the 15th-century Hindu epic, the Mahabharata, as the name of a charioteer of Arjuna
historical_references.context: In the Indian epic Mahabharata, which is believed to have been composed between the 4th and 2nd centuries BCE but the existing versions are primarily from the 14th and 15th centuries, Vihan is mentioned as the name of a charioteer of Arjuna during the great battle of Kurukshetra.
